responsibilities.name: Morning Briefing
responsibilities.instruction: Compile and deliver a morning briefing for the user. Include today's calendar events, unread important emails, and any pending action items from previous days.

context.purpose: Give the user a comprehensive start-of-day overview so they can prioritize effectively and catch anything that needs immediate attention.
process: STEP 1 — Query today's calendar events using calendar-events for the full day range (midnight to midnight in user's timezone). Note conflicts, back-to-back meetings, and any events without agendas.
STEP 2 — Search Gmail for unread messages using gmail-search with is:unread, limited to the most recent 15. Prioritize emails from known contacts and flag anything marked important or starred.
STEP 3 — Check MEMORY.md for any pending action items, follow-ups, or tasks carried over from previous days.

STEP 4 — Compile the briefing into a structured format: (1) Today's Schedule with times and attendees, (2) Priority Emails needing response, (3) Pending Action Items with deadlines, (4) Conflicts or Alerts.
STEP 5 — Deliver the briefing to the user. If there are calendar conflicts or urgent items, highlight them prominently at the top.
context.success_criteria: User receives a well-structured briefing before their workday starts, with all calendar events listed, important emails surfaced, and action items tracked. No surprises missed.
context.prior_learnings: Always convert times to the user's local timezone. Check both primary and secondary calendars if configured. Unread count can be high — focus on emails from the last 24 hours and prioritize by sender importance.

responsibilities.name: End-of-Day Follow-Up Check
responsibilities.instruction: Review the day's activity for unanswered follow-ups, pending drafts, and incomplete tasks. Compile a summary and flag anything that needs attention tomorrow.

context.purpose: Ensure nothing falls through the cracks at the end of the workday. Catch unanswered emails, unsent drafts, and incomplete tasks before they become overdue.
process: STEP 1 — Search Gmail for drafts created today using gmail-search with in:drafts. List any drafts that were created but never sent — these may need follow-up.
STEP 2 — Search for emails sent today that haven't received replies yet, especially those with explicit questions or action requests. Use gmail-search with from:me and today's date range.
STEP 3 — Review MEMORY.md for any tasks or action items that were due today but not marked complete.
STEP 4 — Check tomorrow's calendar for early-morning meetings that might need prep tonight.
STEP 5 — Compile findings into a structured EOD summary: (1) Unsent Drafts, (2) Awaiting Replies, (3) Incomplete Tasks, (4) Tomorrow's Early Events. Deliver to user with recommended next actions.
context.success_criteria: User receives a concise EOD summary highlighting loose ends. All unsent drafts are surfaced, unanswered follow-ups are flagged, and tomorrow's early commitments are previewed.
context.prior_learnings: Keep the EOD summary brief — users want a quick scan, not a lengthy report. Focus on actionable items only. If nothing is outstanding, say so explicitly rather than padding the report.
